newsitem.title: USA: Hollywood Park set on acquisition track.
newsitem.headline: Hollywood Park set on acquisition track.

text.p: With a merger nearly complete and a Los Angeles card club up-and-running, racetrack operator Hollywood Park Inc has firmly repositioned itself as a gaming company with plans to grow through acquisition.
After recent shareholder approvals, the company needs only state licenses to close its merger with Boomtown Inc.

"Boomtown puts Hollywood Park squarely on a path of gaming development," Michael Finnegan, chief financial officer, told Reuters at Friday's grand opening of the Raddisson Crystal Park Hotel & Casino in Compton, a suburb south of Los Angeles.

Crystal Park Hotel & Casino is Hollywood Park's second card club in Los Angeles. In November 1995, it began operating the card club next to its Hollywood Park thoroughbred race track in west Los Angeles. The company has pumped about $36 million into Hollywood Park, and it currently brings in about $800,000 to $900,000 in cash flow per month, Finnegan said.

Hollywood Park invested about $26.5 million to improve the land and refurbish Crystal Park. It leases the hotel/casino to Compton Entertainment Inc for a fee that escalates over time. After its second year, Hollywood Park will make return on its investment of about $9.0 million a year, Finnegan said.

Under California law, the casino operates only card games with the house dealing and supervising. Before today's 1100 PST/1400 EST grand opening, about 28 table games were open and all but two were filled with gamblers.

Though it is in Compton, a neighborhood with a reputation for crime, Crystal Park's location is in a relatively safe industrial and commercial section of the suburb along a major freeway with 50 acres for future business development.
"This area is the last place in the world people think about when they think about Compton," Finnegan said from the tree-lined and well-lit parking lot.
The club targets gamblers coming from Orange County, the affluent county south of Los Angeles. It has 282 hotel rooms and 41 suites, making it the only hotel/casino in Los Angeles.
Its two chief competitors, the Commerce Club and the Bicycle Club, cater to east Los Angeles. The Hollywood Park Casino targets gamblers in west Los Angeles, Finnegan said.
The card clubs and Boomtown's casinos give Hollywood Park a base from which to expand when the Boomtown merger is completed, which is expected in 1997's first quarter.
"There is no question, (we have) an acquisition strategy," Finnegan said.

"We'd look at companies like Boomtown that have operating and already-licensed properties in...any non-Las Vegas, non-Atlantic City markets," he said, adding the cost of entry in those two traditional markets is currently too high.

When it merges with Boomtown, Hollywood Park gets three casinos -- one well-established property in Reno, Nevada, a second in the hot, Biloxi, Mississippi market and a third near New Orleans, which was recently re-approved by voters.
Boomtown is currently developing a casino in Indiana with Hilton Hotels Corp. As a condition of the merger, Boomtown will sell its money-losing operation in Las Vegas.
Finally, Finnegan said it might take two to three more quarters for earnings, which rebounded in the third quarter, to show the kind of stability that pleases investors and boosts the stock price.
But already some Wall Street gamblers are beginning to take note. Shares of Hollywood Park traded as low as 7-5/8 in early October, but on Friday the stock closed at 11-3/4.
